metadata.notes: The SECOND stage of the tortilla-de-patatas-con-cebolla chain (see data/actions/combine_potato_onion.json for the first stage). Target: potato_onion_mixture (already fried, isCombinableBase). Secondary: egg_cracked (isCombinableAddition — the SAME capability data/actions/combine.json's own secondary check uses, deliberately reused rather than given a third dedicated flag, since egg's role here is identical to the onion-free recipe: beaten egg poured over an already-fried base. See data/entities/potato_onion_mixture.json's capabilityAmbiguityNote for the real, named risk this reuse creates.
metadata.toolNote: requiredTools: ['bowl'] — same real technique as combine.json (pour the beaten egg over the fried mixture in a bowl before returning it to the pan), unlike combine_potato_onion.json's tool-free first stage.
metadata.scopeNote: Same fixed-pairing discipline as combine.json's own scopeNote: requiredTargetCapability/requiredSecondaryCapability/combinesInto are FIXED to this one specific combination (potato_onion_mixture + egg -> tortilla_mixture_con_cebolla), not a generalization of COMBINE into a lookup system. A future third variant (e.g. adding bell pepper) would define its own action the same way this one was added alongside combine.json rather than either being touched.
metadata.actionKindNote: Song, Huang, Sun, Tian, Wang & Li, arXiv:2608.04768 (2026, PAPER_NOTES_2608.04768.md, REFERENCES.md): same reasoning as combine.json's identical note — a single one-off assembly of two instances into one; both discriminators agree.

verification.description: A single homogeneous mixture present where fried potato-and-onion and beaten egg were a moment ago
